newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-JUBILANT HUBER WINS IN LEIPZIG AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-JUBILANT HUBER WINS IN LEIPZIG AGAIN.

text.p: Germany's Anke Huber came from a set and 3-0 down to retain her Leipzig tennis title with a 5-7 6-3 6-1 victory over Iva Majoli of Croatia on Sunday.
Majoli, seeded third, looked to have the match sewn up until she began to suffer from cramp midway through the second set. Huber, spurred on by the German crowd, took full advantage.
"I couldn't feel my legs any more and didn't have energy left," Majoli explained afterwards. "I gave Anke the chance to come back but even an injury break wouldn't have helped."

Tears were rolling down Majoli's cheeks at one point as she desperately tried to fight. But she could not get anywhere near some blistering passing shots from the fourth-seeded German and won just one more game in the entire match.
"This is a great tournament. I'd love to came back next year," a delighted Huber said. "I was relaxed and I played well. I think I can really move on from here."
Huber may have profited from an unexpected rest day on Saturday, when her semifinal opponent Steffi Graf withdrew because of a knee injury just hours before the match.
The loss of the world number one, who may have to rest for three to four weeks, meant Huber went through to the final by default.
Graf's withdrawal meant Huber had been given a helping hand to the title for the second year in a row. She was awarded it last year when fellow finalist Magdalena Maleeva withdrew beacuse of illness.
